samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because rounding errors introduced during each operation can vary depending on the order of computation. For example, adding a very small number to a large number may result in no change due to limited precision, but the outcome depends on which numbers are added first. As a result, (a + b) + c may yield a different result than a + (b + c) when floating-point arithmetic is used.
